en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: The single most common mistake I see in {city} accounts is a targeting radius drawn around the city. A large share of {city} businesses do not sell to {city}. They sell to farms, mines, processors and contractors spread across the whole province and often well beyond it, and a 50 kilometre radius quietly cuts off most of the people who were going to buy. Fixing the geography is usually a bigger win here than fixing the ads.

Competition for search is genuinely thin. In {industries}, the number of {city} companies running a serious SEO or content programme is small enough that a business willing to publish real answers to real customer questions can take the top of the results in months rather than years. That is not true in Toronto or Vancouver and it will not stay true here forever.

The other thing worth knowing is that {city} buying cycles in the sectors that matter are long and involve several people. Someone researches for weeks, sends a link to a colleague, and a purchase order shows up two months later. Any measurement setup that only credits the last click will make your best channel look like your worst one.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: We sell across the province, not just in {city}. Does a {city} page even apply?
faq.a: It applies, and that gap is most of the value. Businesses in {industries} routinely sell province-wide while their advertising is targeted at the city they happen to sit in. The first thing I would look at is whether your targeting matches your actual service area, because that mismatch costs more than anything else on the account.

faq.q: Is there enough search volume here to bother?
faq.a: For most {city} businesses, yes, but the honest answer is that it depends on what you sell and I would rather look than guess. On a call I will tell you if I think the volume is too thin to justify paid search. In smaller markets the answer is sometimes that SEO and AIO are worth doing and Google Ads is not, and that is a fine outcome.

faq.q: How long before we see anything?
faq.a: Google Ads can shift within weeks because you are buying attention directly. SEO is a few months before it compounds, which is genuinely fine here because your competitors are not moving fast either. AIO is a one-time piece of work and shows up as soon as the models re-crawl.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
